sources.citation: Zahirovic, S. et al. (2015), Tectonic speed limits from plate kinematic reconstructions, Earth and Planetary Science Letters 418, 40–52.
sources.population: Mesozoic–Cenozoic Earth plate/continent reconstruction samples, multiple plates and reference-frame comparison
sources.scale: Global plate and continental RMS speeds over geological time

evidence.global_plate_rms: approximately 5–10 cm/yr across analyzed Mesozoic-Cenozoic model
evidence.continental_fraction_effect: >50% continental area plates reach approximately 10 cm/yr maximum RMS in their analysis; plate speeds also depend on subducting perimeter, cratonic fraction and reference frame

sources.r6_use: Broad Earth-like plausibility prior only; no per-plate speed assignment and no actual Earth trajectory/rotation reuse.
sources.transfer_justification: R6 is intentionally Earth-scale/Earth-like, so order-of-magnitude and dependence direction inform sanity bounds; synthetic plate geometry, no mantle model, and unknown subduction state prevent direct calibration.
sources.limitations: Reconstruction-dependent statistic, not a universal physical speed cap; absolute frame sensitivity and individual plate heterogeneity remain.

sources.citation: Argus, D. F. (1991), No-net-rotation model of current plate velocities incorporating plate motion model NUVEL-1, Geophysical Research Letters 18, 2039–2042.
sources.population: Present-day Earth plate motions using NUVEL-1 relative velocities

evidence.definition: NNR frame requires no net rotation of lithosphere while retaining specified relative plate velocities
evidence.caveat: NNR and hotspot frame differ materially; dynamic premise of no-net-torque is not guaranteed

sources.r6_use: Supports NNR as a gauge convention to remove arbitrary common rotation, not as mantle truth.
sources.transfer_justification: A synthetic sphere also has an arbitrary common rigid-rotation degree of freedom when only relative plate geometry is modeled; zeroing its area-weighted mean is a transparent coordinate/gauge choice.
sources.limitations: Earth's physical interpretation and weights do not transfer; R6 explicitly makes no mantle-fixed or torque-balance claim.

sources.citation: DeMets, C., Gordon, R. G., Argus, D. F. & Stein, S. (1994), Effect of recent revisions to the geomagnetic reversal time scale on estimates of current plate motions, Geophysical Research Letters 21, 2191–2194.
sources.population: Present-day Earth relative plate motions recalibrated against spreading and geodetic rates

evidence.result: NUVEL-1 angular velocities rescaled by alpha=0.9562 to produce NUVEL-1A; comparison with geodetic rates reduced average discrepancy below 2%

sources.units: dimensionless calibration factor and angular velocities
sources.r6_use: Evidence that even familiar plate-rate models are tied to explicit observations/time-scale calibration; not a source of R6 initial rates.
sources.limitations: Modern Earth relative kinematics; no synthetic plate data or 210 Ma t0 calibration.

sources.citation: Iaffaldano, G., Bodin, T. & Sambridge, M. (2012), Reconstructing plate-motion changes in the presence of finite-rotations noise, Nature Communications 3, 1048.
sources.population: Earth ocean-ridge finite-rotation observations with hierarchical Bayesian noise treatment
sources.scale: Plate-motion temporal change resolution; global ridge reconstruction observations

evidence.result: After noise treatment, inferred plate-motion changes occur on timescales no shorter than a few million years

sources.r6_use: A caution against resolving unjustified sub-few-Myr kinematic jumps; motivates event/displacement-aware segments rather than a fixed dt.
sources.transfer_justification: The signal-processing issue of finite-rotation noise is relevant to any piecewise kinematic representation; it does not prescribe R6 event times.
sources.limitations: Not a universal physical minimum/maximum segment duration; Earth ridge data and their noise model, not synthetic R6.

sources.citation: Brune, S. et al. (2023), Geodynamics of continental rift initiation and evolution, Nature Reviews Earth & Environment 4, 235–253.
sources.population: Earth continental rift observations and geodynamic studies across diverse settings

evidence.result: Inherited weaknesses are exploited; competing drivers/resistance make initiation and localization dynamic; success/failure mechanisms remain debated; successful rifts may show order-of-magnitude divergence increase after sufficient weakening

sources.units: qualitative process synthesis; approximately tenfold ratio reported for a successful-rift behavior, not a threshold
sources.r6_use: Supports separating eligibility, trigger, maturation and realization; supports UNKNOWN weakness and forbids a universal convenience threshold.
sources.transfer_justification: Mechanism-level lessons are relevant to Earth-like continental lithosphere; no numeric threshold is transferred to R6.
sources.limitations: Highly setting-dependent; does not specify a reduced global synthetic R6 scalar law.

sources.citation: Bastow, I. D. & Keir, D. (2009), The enigma of the Ethiopian rift system, and broader rift observations summarized in Corti (2009), Continental rift evolution: From rift initiation to incipient break-up in the Main Ethiopian Rift, Earth-Science Reviews 96, 1–53.
sources.population: Main Ethiopian Rift and Afar/East African region
sources.scale: Regional rift, fault and magmatic evolution

evidence.result: Rift initiation is attributed to reactivation of inherited lithospheric weakness under relative plate extension; evolution includes diachronous and punctuated phases

sources.units: regional geologic times and extension rates; no global transferable trigger value used
sources.r6_use: Mechanistic illustration that inherited orientation and far-field extension interact, and that propagation need not be smooth.
sources.limitations: One tectonic setting, with magmatism and regional boundary forcing; not a global prior or synthetic-world threshold.

sources.citation: pyGPlates 1.0.0 API documentation, FiniteRotation and Primer.
sources.population: Software API semantics, not an Earth parameter population
sources.scale: Spherical rigid plate finite rotations and reconstruction hierarchy

evidence.result: Finite rotation is represented by Euler pole plus angular distance; plate motions are relative rotations organized in a reconstruction tree.

sources.units: pole coordinates and radians for angular distance; time coordinates supplied to model
sources.r6_use: Supports the representation/interface only; no motion parameter, causal law or rift rule is derived from API behavior.
sources.transfer_justification: Mathematical representation applies to spherical rigid transforms independent of geography.
sources.limitations: Software specification is not scientific parameter authority; R6 adapter unvalidated.

sources.citation: Müller, R. D. et al. (2018), GPlates: Building a Virtual Earth Through Deep Time, Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 19, 2243–2261.
sources.population: GPlates reconstruction workflows and example Earth models
sources.scale: Global plate topology and regional deforming plate reconstruction

evidence.result: Time-dependent plate boundary topologies and deforming zones are user/model supplied and used to resolve reconstructions; deformation geometry is based on geological/geophysical evidence in applications.

sources.r6_use: Supports adapter boundary and the distinction between topology-resolving software and authority for topology/kinematics.
sources.transfer_justification: Software architecture is reusable; feature and motion histories from Earth models are not transferred.
sources.limitations: Does not generate R6 causal physics or infer an authoritative vector partition from R6's coarse categorical raster.

parameter_rows.semantics: Per-plate motion in a spherical common gauge frame
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: Earth comparator: continental RMS typically ~3 cm/yr, excursions ~5–6 cm/yr; broad category statistics only
parameter_rows.units: cm/yr RMS comparator; canonical angular rate rad/yr
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Mesozoic-Cenozoic Earth reconstructions, plus modern relative model method
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Earth-like order-of-magnitude plausibility, not synthetic plate direction or velocity assignment
parameter_rows.notes: Gauge removes least-squares common rigid rotation from area-weighted surface velocities, not the simple mean of plate angular vectors. Need adjacency, boundary state, per-plate geometry and outcome-blind joint realization; speed prior cannot assign Euler poles.

parameter_rows.value_range_prior: Earth reconstruction method resolves robust changes no shorter than a few Myr after noise reduction; not a universal segment bound
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Use only to avoid implausible numerical resolution of noise-like changes; R6 adopts hybrid earliest-event/displacement/law-validity condition
parameter_rows.notes: No finite upper bound; no fixed segment length selected.

parameter_rows.semantics: Causal evolution of plate rotation/rate across segment boundaries
parameter_rows.units: angular acceleration/rate change units depend on selected law
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Earth reconstructed changes and forcing associations
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Evidence shows real changes and noise sensitivity, but does not identify an ARCANA reduced causal transition law
parameter_rows.notes: Must condition on governed events/drivers and memory; no random walk.

parameter_rows.semantics: Spherical topological support corresponding to t0 plate labels
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No new geologic resolution; exact spherical union of existing 1-degree cells only
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: A deterministic cell-union is representational conversion of existing support, not inferred finer geology
parameter_rows.uncertainty: COARSE_SUPPORT_ON_FINE_GRID; boundary uncertainty no finer than source cells
parameter_rows.notes: Contract can be bound; materialization/closure checks remain an implementation prerequisite.

parameter_rows.semantics: Inherited mechanical weakness relevant to rift localization
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No scalar or categorical strength transferable to this synthetic mosaic
parameter_rows.units: UNBOUND; dimensionless class not yet justified
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Diverse Earth continental rifts, including regional examples
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Mechanism is transferable, weakness locations/strengths are not; R6 t0 labels are design categories only
parameter_rows.notes: UNKNOWN cannot make eligibility false or trigger true; rift remains UNKNOWN and cannot execute.

parameter_rows.value_range_prior: Defined observable derived from authorized plate kinematics; no current value
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Geometric relative velocity projection is representation-independent; it is not a stress/weakness or a rift threshold
parameter_rows.uncertainty: Propagated from plate-motion and boundary uncertainty
parameter_rows.notes: Equation and units bound; numerical state not computable until P01/P04 are bound/materialized.

parameter_rows.semantics: Three-valued predicate over supported weakness, opening and persistence
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No numeric threshold bound; known false can yield INELIGIBLE, all supported true yield ELIGIBLE, otherwise UNKNOWN
parameter_rows.units: Input-specific; extension m/year; persistence time unit selected by law
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Mechanism and uncertainty semantics transfer; threshold does not

parameter_rows.semantics: Eligible sustained forcing to initiation event
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No universal threshold/hazard supported for R6
parameter_rows.units: Would require strain/extension and time if selected
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Rift systems with divergent mechanisms and outcomes
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Review highlights transient, competing process controls and unresolved tipping points
parameter_rows.notes: Do not initiate stochastically independent of physical eligibility.

parameter_rows.semantics: Rift event to new boundary, plate child lineage and crust/domain consequences
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No global synthetic fragment-size or continuity threshold sourced
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Earth rift scales vary by lithosphere and forcing; GPlates is a representation tool
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: No local/regional rift scale can be promoted to global R6 topology rule without scaling authority
parameter_rows.notes: No event deferral because t0 eligibility cannot currently be evaluated.

parameter_rows.semantics: Deterministic support-aware t0 event classification without event creation
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Governance/schema rule, not an Earth-derived value
parameter_rows.notes: Not executable until master partition, kinematics, weakness and driver states are available.

parameter_rows.semantics: Largest valid timestep under motion, solver error, topology and event crossing constraints
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No solver precision or feature scale bound, therefore no numeric tolerance
parameter_rows.units: time, radians, metres, normalized solver error as applicable
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Reconstruction temporal support is not solver error tolerance
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Method supports caution around temporal aliasing, not a numerical dt value
parameter_rows.notes: Need pinned adapter precision, source-cell support, process timescale and restart equivalence before tolerance selection.

parameter_rows.semantics: Class, interval/distribution only if evidenced, provenance and outcome-blind canonical realization
parameter_rows.value_range_prior: No probability distributions invented; retain reported intervals and UNKNOWN
parameter_rows.earth_population_setting: Uncertainty differs by reconstruction data/time/frame and process
parameter_rows.transfer_justification: Preserve uncertainty epistemically; do not make synthetic world appear uniquely inferred
parameter_rows.notes: No trajectory generated; canonical parameters not selected.
